title: An efficient method for the construction of artificial, concatemeric DNA, RNA and proteins with genetically programmed functions, using a novel, vector-enzymatic DNA fragment amplification-expression technology
author: Skowron, Krawczun, et al.

steps.title: Design synthetic DNA fragment
steps.instruction: Design a double‑stranded synthetic DNA fragment encoding the desired bioactive peptide and flank it with two convergent SapI recognition sites (5′‑GCTCTTC‑3′) so that SapI cleavage will generate 3‑nt 5′ overhangs CCC/GGG for head‑to‑tail ligation. Include at least three base pairs upstream of each SapI site and add GC clamps (G or C in the last three bases of each oligonucleotide) to improve SapI cleavage and PCR efficiency.

steps.title: Optimize codon usage
steps.instruction: Optimize the peptide‑coding DNA sequence for efficient expression in Escherichia coli using a suitable codon‑optimization tool.

steps.title: Synthesize designed DNA
steps.instruction: Order chemical synthesis of the designed DNA fragment de novo from a commercial provider.

steps.title: Generate DNA monomer
steps.instruction: Prepare a suitable amount of the DNA monomer for concatemerization by either (a) PCR with forward and reverse primers that contain SapI sites and generate the required 5′ overhangs, followed by SapI cleavage and purification, or (b) cloning the synthetic fragment into the amplification‑expression vector using SapI sites (or blunt‑end cloning into a SapI or SmaI site followed by fill‑in with dCTP/dGTP). Transform E. coli, verify correct orientation by sequencing, purify plasmid DNA, perform SapI cleavage, separate fragments by electrophoresis, and isolate the desired fragment by electroelution or a commercial kit (e.g., Minute™ Protein/Nucleic Extraction Kit, Invent Biotechnologies). For high purity, follow the gel‑extracted fragment with phenol:chloroform extraction and ethanol precipitation.

steps.title: Perform SapI cleavage
steps.instruction: Incubate the purified DNA monomer with SapI for 2 h at 37 °C in a reaction containing 20 mM Tris‑acetate (pH 7.9 at 25 °C), 10 mM magnesium acetate, 50 mM potassium acetate, 100 µg ml⁻¹ BSA, 20 µg DNA fragment and 5 U SapI. Inactivate the enzyme by heating 20 min at 65 °C. (Optional: use the SapI isoschizomers BspQI or LguI according to the manufacturer’s instructions.)

steps.title: Purify SapI fragments
steps.instruction: Separate the SapI restriction fragments on a 10 % polyacrylamide gel in TBE buffer, excise the band containing the desired fragment, and purify it by electroelution or a commercial DNA purification kit. Store the purified fragment on ice for the ligation step.

steps.title: First directional autoligation
steps.instruction: Set up an autoligation reaction with 1.5 µg purified SapI‑cleaved fragment in a total volume of 72 µl containing 0.01 Weiss U T4 DNA ligase and ligation buffer (40 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.8 at 25 °C, 10 mM MgCl₂, 10 mM DTT, 0.5 mM ATP). Incubate at 16 °C and withdraw 5 µl aliquots at 5, 10, 20, 40, 80 and 160 min for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Analyse each time‑point by polyacrylamide or agarose electrophoresis; a ladder of increasing DNA lengths indicates formation of directional concatemers.
Purify the concatemer(s) of the desired length from the gel.
Clone the purified concatemer into a SapI‑linearized, dephosphorylated vector (preferably pre‑treated with thermolabile Shrimp Alkaline Phosphatase, SAP).

steps.title: Clone concatemer into vector
steps.instruction: Perform a ligation with 540 ng autoligated insert, 270 ng SapI‑linearized/dephosphorylated vector, 1 Weiss U T4 DNA ligase in 90 µl of buffer (40 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.8 at 25 °C, 10 mM MgCl₂, 10 mM DTT, 0.5 mM ATP). Incubate at 16 °C for 16 h.

steps.title: Transform and select E. coli
steps.instruction: Purify the ligation mixture and transform electrocompetent E. coli cells (recommended strains: DH5α, Top10, JM109, Endura™). Plate on appropriate antibiotic medium and screen colonies. Verify insert orientation by sequencing if needed.

steps.title: Optional second amplification or expression
steps.instruction: Either (a) use the recombinant construct directly for expression of the concatemeric protein, or (b) subject the construct to another round of SapI cleavage, autoligation and cloning to obtain longer concatemeric genes.

steps.title: Alternative synthetic monomer amplification
steps.instruction: Chemically synthesize a repetitive gene containing several to dozens of peptide‑coding copies, clone it into a SapI‑linearized/dephosphorylated amplification‑expression vector, and treat it as a monomer for the amplification cycle described in steps 4–9.

steps.title: Long‑fragment ligation with PEG4000
steps.instruction: For DNA fragments longer than a short peptide, first prepare a monomer with SapI‑generated CCC/GGG overhangs and gel‑purify it. Autoligate 2 µg monomer in 20 µl containing 40 mM Tris‑HCl (pH 7.8 at 25 °C), 150 mM NaCl, 20 % PEG4000, 10 mM MgCl₂, 10 mM DTT, 0.5 mM ATP and either 0.01 or 0.1 Weiss U T4 DNA ligase. Incubate 16 h at 16 °C, taking 15, 30, 45 and 60 min samples. Combine all reaction products and purify the ligation mixture.

steps.title: Clone long‑fragment ligation mixture
steps.instruction: Ligate the purified mixture into a SapI‑linearized/dephosphorylated vector (e.g., pAMP1‑HisA) in 20 µl containing 40 mM Tris‑HCl (pH 7.8 at 25 °C), 10 mM MgCl₂, 10 mM DTT, 0.5 mM ATP, 400 ng insert, 50 ng vector and 1 Weiss U T4 DNA ligase. Incubate at 22 °C for 1 h, then inactivate ligase at 70 °C for 5 min. Purify the ligation products, ethanol‑precipitate, and transform into E. coli as in step 8.
